summary: Dedicated tenant p99 latency drift during burst pilot; suspected noisy-neighbor impact correlated with burst pool saturation (us-east)
description:
Customer report (via pilot check-in):
- Starting 2025-07-08 ~15:05 PT, they observed intermittent tail latency increase (p99) on their Dedicated tenant while burst was enabled.
- They suspect noisy-neighbor behavior because baseline throughput held but p99 drifted and a subset of requests spiked (timeouts near their client 30s limit).

Impact:
- Increased p99 latency on chat completions; sporadic timeouts during peak window.
- Customer is running a time-boxed pilot and requested confirmation that other tenants cannot degrade their baseline Dedicated performance.

Customer expectation:
- Baseline Dedicated pool should remain isolated.
- If burst pools are saturated, requests should be denied/limited rather than degrade existing SLOs.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: northbridge-prod
- Region: us-east
- Burst enabled: yes (pilot)
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (pinned)

Initial signals from customer:
- Spikes coincide with their weekly batch workflow (predictable load step-up).
- They did not intentionally route traffic to a new model/region.

Requested by customer:
- Confirmation of root cause.
- Guidance for client retry behavior when burst is denied.
- Whether we can add a hard guardrail to stop p99 degradation during burst contention.
comments:
2025-07-08 15:42 PT — Miguel Santos (Reporter)
Opened ticket after customer success call. Customer provided client-side traces showing p99 moved ~1.2s -> ~3.8s for ~20 min. They asked if they were impacted by other burst tenants.

Next steps: pulling internal dashboards and routing traces; looping SRE + fleet + routing. (Also flagged in #incidents.)

2025-07-08 16:10 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Triage: treating as Sev2/P1 due to tail latency regression on dedicated pilot.

Initial checks:
- Dedicated baseline pool for northbridge-prod shows stable GPU utilization; no evidence of over-commit.
- However, request traces indicate a subset of calls were admitted to burst pool (header x-rw-burst-admitted=true) during the same time window.
- Burst pool in us-east shows saturation > 0.92 and admission rejects rising.

Hypothesis: burst pool saturation + queueing increased tail latency for burst-admitted traffic; customer is aggregating p99 across all requests (baseline + burst). Need to confirm they are not mixing in burst-admitted calls in their SLO view.

Action: asked Logan Wright to confirm metrics dimensions and whether we can break out baseline vs burst for this tenant in the pilot dashboard.

2025-07-08 17:05 PT — Peter Holtz (Routing SRE embed)
Looked at routing decision logs for tenant northbridge-prod:
- During 15:03–15:27 PT, baseline pool hit tenant-configured concurrency cap; routing attempted burst.
- Burst admission allowed, but pool had elevated queue depth and kernel scheduling contention.
- No evidence of baseline pool traffic being shifted into shared hosted fleet.

Recommendation: tighten burst admission gate to deny earlier when burst pool saturation > 0.85 (currently 0.92) + apply cooldown so we don't keep sending them into a bad pool. This aligns with the new circuit breaker work (ENG-4828).

2025-07-09 09:18 PT — Sean Gallagher (SRE lead)
Confirmed: baseline isolation intact. The customer’s p99 regression is attributable to burst-admitted traffic experiencing queuing latency under pool saturation.

Key point for comms: Burst is best-effort and must fail closed (deny) under contention. We need to ensure the deny happens early enough to preserve customer expectations.

Mitigation plan (today):
1) Reduce burst pool routing weight in us-east temporarily.
2) Lower saturation threshold for global burst circuit breaker in us-east.
3) Ensure customer has clear deny signals (429/503 + reason codes) and recommended retry/backoff behavior.

Also: observability-pack dashboards already show pool saturation; we need per-tenant baseline vs burst p99 split surfaced to CS for pilots.

2025-07-09 12:02 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Mitigation executed:
- Reduced burst pool weight in us-east by 30%.
- Enabled stricter saturation gate (deny burst admission when saturation > 0.85 for 60s).

After change, burst admission rejects increased (as intended) and burst-admitted tail latency returned to normal range.

Draft customer update:
- Baseline Dedicated pool not impacted by other tenants.
- The elevated p99 came from burst-admitted traffic during burst pool saturation.
- We adjusted gating to deny earlier to avoid queueing.

Need follow-up: docs + error semantics so their client treats burst denies correctly (SUP-3277 reference).

2025-07-10 10:41 PT — Nadia Rahman (Metering)
Confirmed we can attribute baseline vs burst in shadow metering for this tenant. For the incident window, ~18% of requests were burst-admitted. We can provide an internal breakdown; recommend we do not share exact pool utilization with customer, but we can state that a shared burst pool was saturated and admission policy was tightened.

Also flagged that burst-denied responses should be clearly distinguishable in customer metrics to avoid confusing their SLO calculations.

2025-07-11 14:20 PT — Miguel Santos (Customer Success)
Customer acknowledged explanation. They asked for two concrete items:
1) How to identify burst-admitted vs baseline in their own logs.
2) Retry guidance when burst is denied (they currently retry immediately, which can amplify spike).

They also want a recommended default: keep baseline limits as-is but set burst max TPS to X and burst concurrency cap to Y to avoid p99 swings.

Looping docs team and SRE for recommended settings; will follow up by Monday.

2025-07-12 09:05 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Resolution:
- Root cause: burst pool saturation in us-east caused queueing for burst-admitted traffic; customer p99 included those requests. No evidence of baseline Dedicated pool degradation from other tenants.
- Mitigations: tightened saturation gate + applied circuit-breaker behavior to deny burst earlier; reduced routing weight to burst pool in us-east while capacity headroom recovers.
- Customer guidance: use response headers/log fields to separate burst-admitted traffic from baseline; implement exponential backoff on burst-denied responses.

Follow-ups created:
- INT-881: ensure on-call has correct admin permissions to disable burst per tenant quickly.
- SUP-3277: improve customer-facing error semantics + docs.

Marking Resolved; will reopen if p99 drift recurs outside burst-admitted cohort.
resolution: Resolved by confirming baseline isolation, attributing tail latency increase to burst-admitted traffic under burst pool saturation, and tightening burst admission gating (deny earlier) plus temporarily reducing burst pool routing weight in us-east. Provided customer guidance to separate baseline vs burst in metrics and to apply backoff on burst-denied responses.
